coldRead.icp: DON at a 25-bed rural hospital, reading once on a phone

undefinedTerms: cycle (length never pinned down; the math uses a four-week cycle, the seniority example uses a six-week cycle)
"once time off is counted" / the 10.6 and 9.6 nurse figures (derivation lives in another guide)
"the fewest charge-qualified nurses this example needs" (why 6 and 5 is not shown here)
target ("check every nurse's counts against your target", "weekend target next cycle"; never said whether target = the even share, or how it changes for part-timers or carry-over)
Baylor shift (only a link, no gloss)
mondayActions: Work out my own weekend number: 104 x nurses needed per weekend day, divided by my nurses
Go back through last cycle's posted schedules and tally weekend, holiday and charge shifts per nurse
Add a count column to my scheduling spreadsheet before I build the next cycle
List every weekend exemption or day limit with who approved it and a review date
Fill holidays and weekend charge shifts first next build, lowest count first
Post a count sheet next to the schedule
blockedActions: Divide by 'your nurses' when my roster mixes full-time, part-time and PRN: the post never shows how part-timers or PRNs go into the divisor
Set a weekend target for a part-time nurse inside the cycle math (only the yearly half-of-38 example is given)
Carry an extra March weekend into April's build: the post says it should happen but not how (subtract from target? swap first?)
Decide whether picked-up callout shifts lower next cycle's weekend target: listed as a decision to write down, with no guidance either way
Pull last cycle's callout pickups: they are not on the posted schedule, and the post does not say where to find them
Work out how many charge-qualified nurses my unit needs: the post sends me to another guide for that number
